title: Keep order history when the shop exports only what changed

ticket.subject: fct_order_lines will lose history from tomorrow
body: Heads-up: from tomorrow's export (13 March) the new shop platform no longer sends every order line.
It sends every order, but only the **lines created or changed since the previous export**, and the
ingestion replaces `shop_order_lines` in the landing schema each night, as it does today.
`fct_order_lines` is a plain table rebuilt from staging on each run, so after tomorrow's run it will only
hold the lines of one export. Finance reconciles revenue on it every morning.
Can you change it so it keeps every line it has seen, exactly once, and takes corrections into account
(a line can come back with a new discount, and a line can be added to an old order)? Today's full export
is already in the landing schema. Once your version runs, load tomorrow's export with **Load next batch**
and run it again the way the nightly job would.

acceptance.text: fct_order_lines is an incremental model keyed on order_id and line_number.
After tomorrow's run, every order line of both exports is in the fact exactly once.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_lines, count(DISTINCT order_id || '/' || line_number) AS distinct_lines, count(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders FROM dbt_dev_incr.fct_order_lines

acceptance.text: The corrected discount and the late line are in the fact.

checks.sql: SELECT order_id, line_number, net_amount FROM dbt_dev_incr.fct_order_lines WHERE (order_id = 'SO1008' AND line_number = 1) OR (order_id = 'SO1007' AND line_number = 2) ORDER BY 1, 2
checks.fail: A changed or late line is missing or out of date.

acceptance.text: Your last run was a normal (not full-refresh) dbt build, and everything passed.

requires.message: Tomorrow's export has not landed yet: click Load next batch, then run dbt build again.

check.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM incr_raw.shop_orders WHERE order_id = 'SO1011'

hints: Look at what tomorrow's `shop_order_lines` will contain, and at what a table materialization does with it.
An incremental model runs its SQL with `is_incremental()` true once the table exists; `{{ this }}` is the table itself.
Which column tells you a line is new or changed: the order date, or the time the export landed?
A unique_key can be a list of columns; with dbt-duckdb's default strategy (delete+insert) a changed line replaces the old one.
